answer: Make one vote cost more as the swarm grows. Concretely, an agent's attestation weight is capped by how many distinct operators have bonded for it, and the bond for a fresh key is priced against the funding cluster it shares, so keys traced to one wallet pay a rising deposit. The consensus kernel rejects any quorum where one funder supplies too large a share of voting keys. An attacker cloning ten thousand addresses pays a bill that steepens with every shell, while an honest agent commits once; velvet masks stay cheap, but saffron-priced collateral behind them does not.
